name: Barbados
peoples: Earlier Indigenous communities; no established settlement at English arrival
summary: A remarkably steady line through a turbulent region.
notes: Earlier Indigenous occupation is well established, but its chronology and population at European contact should not be flattened into a continuous Kalinago state. Barbados became a republic in 2021, fifty-five years after independence.

events.title: Early European encounters
events.detail: Portuguese and Spanish voyages are associated with early sightings; neither established durable colonial government.
events.uncertainty: Dates and attributions vary. No invented Spanish ownership interval is assigned.

events.title: An English claim
events.detail: John Powell claimed Barbados before permanent settlement.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: English colony established
events.detail: Settlers arrived under a proprietary venture; plantation slavery transformed the island.

events.title: Parliamentary authority imposed
events.detail: An English fleet ended royalist resistance; this changed the regime, not the imperial power.

events.title: Barbados becomes independent
events.detail: The former colony became a sovereign state.

events.title: A republic within the Commonwealth
events.detail: A president replaced the monarch as head of state; independence dated from 1966.
